title: Glasgow-Blatchford Bleeding Score
sources: Blatchford O et al. Lancet 2000; NICE / ACG upper-GI-bleed guidance (GBS ≤ 1 → consider outpatient management)
purpose: Pre-endoscopy risk stratification for acute upper GI bleeding — identifies who is low-risk enough for outpatient management vs. who needs admission and urgent endoscopy. Uses only clinical data and labs (no endoscopy findings).

interpretation.label: Low risk — very low need for transfusion, endoscopic intervention, or death. Consider outpatient management with early outpatient endoscopy
Intermediate risk — admit, resuscitate, endoscopy within 24 h
High risk — active resuscitation, blood products as needed, urgent endoscopy; a score ≥ 12 predicts the highest need for intervention

notes: GBS 0 (or ≤ 1 in some protocols) is the threshold for considering discharge without inpatient endoscopy in a haemodynamically stable patient with no other reason to admit. The score does not incorporate anticoagulant use — factor that in separately.
buildNote: Additive with graded lab bands. Score range 0–23.
